The outer surface of a steel gear is to be hardened by increasing its carbon content; the carbon is to be supplied from an external carbon-rich atmosphere maintained at an elevated temperature. A diffusion heat treatment at $600^{\circ} \mathrm{C}(873 \mathrm{~K})$ for 100 min increases the carbon concentration to $0.75 \mathrm{wt} \%$ at a position 0.5 mm below the surface. Estimate the diffusion time required at $900^{\circ} \mathrm{C}(1173 \mathrm{~K})$ to achieve this same concentration also at a 0.5 mm position. Assume that the surface carbon content is the same for both heat treatments, which is maintained constant. Use the diffusion data in  table 6.2  for $C$ diffusion in $\alpha-F e$.


Table 6.2
A Tabulation of Diffusion Data
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Diffusing Species & Host Metal & $D_0\left(m^2 / s\right)$ & $Q_d(\mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol})$ \\
\hline \multicolumn{4}{|c|}{Interstitial Diffusion} \\
\hline $\mathrm{C}^b$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\alpha$ or BCC $){ }^a$ & $1.1 \times 10^{-6}$ & 87,400 \\
\hline $\mathrm{C}^c$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\gamma \text { or FCC })^a$ & $2.3 \times 10^{-5}$ & 148,000 \\
\hline $\mathrm{N}^b$ & $\mathrm{Fe}(\alpha$ or BCC$){ }^a$ & $5.0 \times 10^{-7}$ & 77,000 \\

\hline & \multicolumn{3}{|c|}{Self-Diffusion} \\

## Reasoning

For carburization with constant surface concentration, the solution to Fick's second law gives:

$$\frac{C_x - C_0}{C_s - C_0} = 1 - \text{erf}\!\left(\frac{x}{2\sqrt{Dt}}\right)$$

Since the **same concentration** is to be achieved at the **same position** with the **same surface and initial concentrations**, the left-hand side is identical for both treatments. Thus the argument of the error function must be equal:

$$\frac{x}{2\sqrt{D_1 t_1}} = \frac{x}{2\sqrt{D_2 t_2}} \;\Longrightarrow\; D_1 t_1 = D_2 t_2$$

$$t_2 = \frac{D_1 t_1}{D_2}$$

The diffusion coefficient follows $D = D_0\exp(-Q_d/RT)$. For C in α-Fe: $D_0 = 1.1\times10^{-6}\,\text{m}^2/\text{s}$, $Q_d = 87400\,\text{J/mol}$.

- At $T_1 = 873\,\text{K}$: $D_1 = 6.45\times10^{-12}\,\text{m}^2/\text{s}$
- At $T_2 = 1173\,\text{K}$: $D_2 = 1.40\times10^{-10}\,\text{m}^2/\text{s}$

$$t_2 = \frac{(6.45\times10^{-12})(100)}{1.40\times10^{-10}} \approx 4.59\,\text{min}$$

$$\boxed{4.6}$$
